To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the co-occurrence of the mutations in the genes encoding TET2 and FLT3ITD in AML patients, and in a mouse model of AML, is associated with epigenetic repression (by DNA methylation and histone deacetylation) of the tumor suppressor gene RUNX3, encoding a Wnt antagonist, and with overexpression of ID1 (a Wnt agonist) and of the homeobox gene HOXA9, and that these effects are reversible

the combination of Sorafenib/Vorinostat/Bortezomib induces a response in relapsed AML, including FltITD+ve patients, that is associated with epigenetic changes, including de-repression of Wnt antagonist, RUNX3, downregulation of ID1, and HOXA repression, and is associated with concurrent TET2 and Flt3 mutation/hypomorhy.

epigenetically-driven dysregulation of HOXA and Wnt pathways is a critical feature of AML and that epigenetically active agent combinations, including histone deacetylases, can be used to target this dysregulation and to restore normal gene expression in the disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of a novel epigenetic phenotype in AML, involving Wnt pathway antagonism, and the development of a novel epipenomenal therapeutic strategy, involving combinations of targeted agents, which can be used for the management of this subset of patients with AML, including Flt-3ITD+ AML.

the development of epigenetically-based combination therapy, targeting distinct effectors of signal transduction and histone deacetylases, in relapsed AML’s, in particular Flt3ITDs, with a signature of epigenetic repression, including Wnt antagonist RUN3, in context of TET2 mutation, and HOXA overexpression.

a novel epigenetic phenotype in relapsed AML’s with Flt3ITDs, which is associated with a distinct pattern of epigenetic dysregulation, including RUNX/TET/ID1/HOXA, and which can be targeted with a novel combination of agents, which is associated in turn with a strikingly high rate of response, and with a novel mechanism of action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the epigenetically-active combination of Sorafenib, Vorinostat, and Bortezomih, in relapsed and/or refractory adult AML, is effective and safe, and that it is associated with early and significant pharmacodynamic changes in patient blasts in situ.

epigenetically-active agents, acting on both signal transduction (Flt3/Raf inhibitors) and chromatin remodeling (histone deacetylases), can be combined to achieve rapid and durable remissions in adult AML, including relapsed/refractor cases.

epigenetically-active combinations of agents acting on distinct pathways, at the levels involving both signal transduction (Raf/Flt3) and chromatin remodeling (histone deacetylases, proteasome inhibition) are effective for relapsed/refratory Flt3ITDs+ve AMLs, in which Wnt pathway dysregulated epigenetic phenotype, including RUNX/TET2/ID1/HOXA, is present.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

epigenetic dysregulation of Wnt pathway antagonist genes, RUNX3 and HOXA, is a common feature among adult AML, and that this can be targeted by combination of epigenetically-active agents, including histone deacetylases inhibitors, to achieve objective remissions, in context of concurrent Flt3ITDs and TET2 mutation.

epigenetically-active combination agents can be used to treat AML, in a manner that is dependent upon the epigenetically-active agents’ ability to reverse epigenetic silencing and to induce epigenetic de-repression, of Wnt antagonist genes.

epigenetically-active agents, acting in concert, may be effective for AML, including relapsed/refractoriness, by targeting distinct pathways, including ID1-RUN-X3-TET2-HOXA, with a potential for synergy, as well as for individual agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Wnt signaling pathway plays a key role in AML pathogenesis and that the epigenetic reprogramming of the Wnt antagonist, RUNX3, is an important target in AML therapy.
the Wnt signaling pathway is a critical effector of AML, and is dysregulated by TET2 and Flt3 ITD mutations.
the epigenetic phenotype, involving ID1 and HOX dysregulation, is a common and important feature of adult AML.
